+== FAQ
+
+=== Why do I get different result when type checking with different configurations?
+
+The IDL compiler can only _completely_ type check IDL code when all parameters are known.
+There are two reasons why some type errors may be caught in one context but not the other.
+
+First, without known parameter values, then types like `Bits<MXLEN>` have an unknown (though, in
+this case, bounded) width.
+When some parameter values are not known, the IDL compiler type checking is best effort.
+It checks as much as it can given the known values.
+It does value analysis to try to bound the problem (like the example above) in order to provide as
+much feedback as possible without knowning all values.
+But, generally, when it can't prove that there is type error, it reports nothing.
+
+Second, when type checking with some known values, the compiler has to do some value analysis to know
+which paths are impossible. Take the following code:
+
+[source,idl]
+----
+if (xlen() == 32) {
+  CSR[mstatush].MPV = 1;
+} else {
+  CSR[mstatus].MPV = 1;
+}
+----
+
+When xlen() is 64, the 'then' path would be a type error because `mstatush` doesn't exist.
+Thus, with known values, unreachable paths are not type checked at all.
+If the above example had a real type error but was checked in the context of a config that can never
+have xlen() == 32, the type error would not be reported.
+
+In general, a best practice is to always type check the unconfig _and_ type check for any
+configuration(s) that you care about.
